customer_jane: Hey team, hitting 401 invalid_api_key from the API intermittently since yesterday. Some requests succeed and others fail with:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_api_key",
    "message": "Invalid API key provided"
  }
}
```
Happens from our lambda (Node) and also when my coworker curls from her laptop. Not seeing anything in the dashboard about revoked keys. Any ideas? :confused:

maria_support: Thanks for the report — can you paste the exact curl or code you're running (with the key redacted)? Also which header are you passing? We sometimes see people mixing `Authorization: Bearer` vs `x-api-key` depending on SDK/route. :eyes:

customer_jane: Sure — here's the curl we run in CI (key replaced with <REDACTED>):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hi"}'
```
And our lambda uses the official SDK with `client.apiKey = process.env.REDWOOD_KEY` (Node). The env var is set in AWS console.

ingram_dev: Two quick checks: 1) Is the key rotated recently? 2) Any chance the env var has quotes/newlines? Using `console.log(JSON.stringify(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY).length)` often catches trailing CRLF.

customer_jane: We rotated keys last week as part of a scheduled rotation. But dashboard shows the old key still listed as active? I can check. Also tried `Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key` — both give 401 sometimes. Very weird.

maria_support: If you're using the hosted API, the supported pattern is `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` (or SDK). `x-api-key` should work for legacy endpoints but can be inconsistent across routes. The intermittent part suggests something like: cached function with old key, or a proxy/loadbalancer rewriting headers, or a key with limited scopes. Can you run the curl with `-v` to see headers and share (redact key)?

customer_jane: Ran verbose curl. Header shows `Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>` on failing requests as well. CLI output: `> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1` and our app logs show `401 invalid_api_key` with request IDs.

sre_oncall: Also check for preflight or OPTIONS requests if a browser was involved — proxies sometimes drop Authorization on OPTIONS. But since it's server-side lambda and curl, probably not CORS. Another thing: If you have multiple keys (old/new) and a CDN caching layer, old key results might be cached somewhere and subsequent requests hit different edge nodes with old key revoked.

customer_jane: Hmm we do have a short TTL CloudFront in front of our service for static assets, but the API calls go directly to Redwood. No CDN. We do have an internal proxy that adds additional headers — maybe it's stripping Authorization sometimes.

maria_support: Can you also try the raw Authorization header value length check? Some SDKs wrap keys with quotes if sourced from a `.env` and you end up sending "sk_abc..." which fails. To test quickly: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" )" ...` vs `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" ...`

customer_jane: Good call. I cat'ed the secret from AWS Parameter Store and it indeed has a trailing newline. When I `printf "%s" "$KEY" | xxd` I see `0a` at the end. So that explains some 401s — but weirdly not all requests fail.

ingram_dev: That can cause intermittent failures if some parts of the infra trim trailing whitespace and others don't. For example, server-side LB might trim, while direct worker processes use literal header. Fix by ensuring secrets are stored without newline (use `aws ssm get-parameter --query Parameter.Value --output text` to avoid quotes/newlines) or run `KEY=$(echo -n "$KEY")` in startup.

customer_jane: Removing the newline from the Parameter Store value fixed it for the curl tests — no more 401s locally. However our lambda still shows occasional 401s in the logs (different request IDs). Could those be coming from a rotated-but-still-active older key?

maria_support: Possible. Two suggestions: 1) Check Dashboard -> API Keys to confirm which keys are active and their last-used timestamps. 2) Search your logs for `API-Key` header variants or proxies adding `Authorization` with old value — maybe an old config is deployed in one region. Also verify token scopes/roles if you're using scoped keys; invalid scope yields auth errors on guarded endpoints.

customer_jane: Dashboard shows two keys: `key-2026-rotation` (active) and `key-older` (disabled last week). The last-used for `key-older` shows a few hits yesterday (matching failing request timestamps). So something in our infra is still sending the old key. I'll grep our repos for the old key identifier.

sre_oncall: If you want us to trace request IDs, paste a couple of failing request IDs and we can look at the full header/edge logs from our side and confirm which key was received and why it was rejected. We won't expose the full key. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: Thanks — pasted two request ids to DM (r12345, r12378). Also found an old staging Lambda config that had the old key in environment. Redeploying now.

deploy_bot: deploy succeeded: service/webhook-staging v2026.03.03 — env updated.

maria_support: Great. After redeploy, monitor for 10-15m. If you still see 401s, send the failing request IDs and we'll pull the edge logs. Typical root causes we see: trailing newline/quotes in secret, old key still deployed somewhere, header rewriting by internal proxies, or using the wrong header format (some internal SDKs expect `x-api-key`).

customer_jane: Awesome — redeploy removed the last 401s. Looks like a mix of trailing newline and a forgotten staging env. Appreciate the quick help! :tada:

maria_support: Glad it's resolved — filing a short KB entry on common 401 causes (trailing whitespace, quotes in env, header mismatch, old key still deployed). Will ping once KB is live. :white_check_mark:
